subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should credential-shaped keys explicitly configured in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` be allowed for intended active-skill host exec use, and how should unrelated generic exec children be isolated from those same keys?
rationale: The source and docs support the regression, but the repair changes a credential-to-exec boundary and must be reconciled with the open inverse secret-leak issue before automation can safely choose semantics.

options.title: Scoped allow plus isolation
options.body: Permit explicit active-skill configured env keys for intended skill-owned execution, keep dangerous host override names blocked, and prove unrelated generic exec children do not inherit those secrets.

options.title: Metadata-only allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare sensitive env names in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys are not expected to work.

options.title: Defer to credential contract
options.body: Pause this bypass until maintainers define a broader SecretRef or plugin-owned credential delivery contract for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Scoped allow plus isolation
recommendation.body: Permit explicit active-skill configured env keys for intended skill-owned execution, keep dangerous host override names blocked, and prove unrelated generic exec children do not inherit those secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env and SecretRef repair path.
